name: Hymenaeus
overview: Hymenaeus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, specifically noted for being handed over to Satan by the Apostle Paul as recorded in 1 Timothy 1:20. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His mention is brief but significant in the context of church discipline.
namesAndTitles: The name Hymenaeus appears only once in the biblical record, with no given meaning or divine origin noted. It is simply a proper name without additional title or significance explained in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Hymenaeus beyond what is mentioned in his unique attribute of being handed over to Satan by Paul.
scriptureSignificance: Hymenaeus is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of a believer who was disciplined by Paul for causing division or error within the church. Being handed over to Satan indicates a serious corrective measure aimed at bringing about repentance and maintaining the purity of the Christian community. His case highlights the Apostle Paul's role in safeguarding sound doctrine and church order.
